content: The Ulster Hospital, also referred to as Dundonald Hospital or simply The Ulster, is a medical facility located on the outskirts of East Belfast, Northern Ireland. It provides acute healthcare services to a population of approximately 250,000 people residing in the North Down, Ards, and Castlereagh council areas, as well as East Belfast. Additionally, it serves as one of the four regional cancer units in Northern Ireland. The hospital was originally established in 1872 under the name Ulster Hospital for Women and Sick Children. Its first location was on Chichester Street in Belfast City Centre. Over time, it relocated to Mountpottinger Road and later to Templemore Avenue. During its time at the Mountpottinger site, the hospital sustained significant damage in the 1941 Belfast Blitz. In 1962, the hospital was moved to Dundonald and renamed the Ulster Hospital. For many years, the hospital experienced under-investment. However, in 2001, a seven-year refurbishment program with a budget of £98 million was announced. Initially, there were plans to construct an entirely new hospital, but these plans were eventually abandoned. The redevelopment included upgrades to the Accident & Emergency (A&E) department, the construction of a new maternity block, a critical care unit, and a renal unit. In 2006, the redevelopment plans were revised, and the project was divided into two phases. The total investment was increased to over £340 million by 2016. The updated plans included the addition of seven new operating theatres and a multi-storey car park. The car park, which addressed previous parking shortages, was opened in 2007.
